## Incident Report: NetSupport RAT Infection — 2024-11-26

### 1. Victim Host
| Attribute | Value | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| IPv4 | 10.11.26.183 | Consistent source across all malicious traffic |
| MAC address | d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b | ARP: `arp.src.proto_ipv4==10.11.26.183` |
| Windows hostname | DESKTOP-B8TQK49 | NBNS name registration (`nbns.name`) and DNS queries for `DESKTOP-B8TQK49` / `DESKTOP-B8TQK49.local` |
| Domain/workgroup | NEMOTODES (workgroup), domain controller NEMOTODE-DC / NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health at 10.11.26.3 | NBNS records, DNS SRV lookups for `_ldap._tcp...NEMOTODES-DC.nemotoads.health` |
| Logged-in user | oboomwald | Kerberos `CNameString` in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ exchanges between 10.11.26.183 and DC 10.11.26.3 |

### 2. Malware Family
**NetSupport RAT** (malicious repurposing of the legitimate NetSupport Manager remote-control tool).

**Attribution: signature-confirmed.** The C2 session to 194.180.191.64:443 was plaintext HTTP over the TLS port and decodes cleanly:
```
POST http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm HTTP/1.1
User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3
...
CMD=POLL
INFO=1
ACK=1
```
Server responses identify as `Server: NetSupport Gateway/1.8 (Windows NT)` with `CMD=ENCD` encoded payload beacons. This exact `fakeurl.htm` POST target, `NetSupport Manager/1.3` user-agent, and CMD=POLL/ENCD protocol is the well-documented NetSupport RAT C2 protocol, and matches the Suricata alerts `ETPRO TROJAN NetSupport RAT CnC Activity`, `ETPRO TROJAN Malicious NetSupport Rat CnC Checkin`, and `ET INFO NetSupport Remote Admin Checkin/Response`.

Likely delivery vector: the host resolved and connected to `modandcrackedapk.com` (a cracked-software/mod-APK lure domain, TLS SNI to 193.42.38.139) shortly before the RAT beaconing began, consistent with a fake-download/ClickFix-style infection chain (Suricata: `ET CURRENT_EVENTS ZPHP Domain in DNS Lookup/TLS SNI (modandcrackedapk.com)`). No plaintext file transfer for the initial dropper was captured (delivery occurred over TLS), so no dropper filename/hash can be grounded in this evidence.

### 3. Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoints:**
- `194.180.191.64:443` — primary NetSupport RAT C2, `POST /fakeurl.htm`, CMD=POLL/ENCD beacon traffic (65+ POSTs observed, tcp streams 77 and 140)
- `104.26.1.231:80` — GeoIP lookup, `GET /location/loca.asp` (Host: geo.netsupportsoftware.com), NetSupport RAT geolocation check-in

**Malicious/suspicious domains:**
- `modandcrackedapk.com` → resolves to 193.42.38.139 (DNS A record + TLS SNI observed; likely lure/delivery domain)
- `194.180.191.64` (bare-IP Host header used for C2, no domain)
- `geo.netsupportsoftware.com` → 104.26.1.231 (NetSupport-branded geolocation service, confirms RAT identity)

Secondary domains present in the capture (`classicgrand.com` → 213.246.109.5, `confirmsubscription.com` → 13.56.30.207/52.8.34.0) were also contacted around the infection window and are consistent with known NetSupport RAT/ClickFix redirect chains, but no direct evidence (HTTP content or C2 protocol) ties them to malicious activity in this capture — flagging as **suspicious, not confirmed**.

**Malicious URLs:**
- `http://194.180.191.64/fakeurl.htm` (C2 beacon/check-in endpoint, User-Agent: NetSupport Manager/1.3)
- `http://104.26.1.231/location/loca.asp` (NetSupport geolocation lookup)

**Transferred files / hashes:**
None observed. All objects recoverable via HTTP object export are benign (Windows Update CAB files, `connecttest.txt`, Adobe `ProcessMAU.txt`, OCSP responses). The NetSupport RAT C2 channel itself carries only encoded `CMD=ENCD` data blobs (RC4/XOR-obfuscated), not file transfers, in the captured window — no SHA256 or filename can be grounded for the payload/dropper itself.

### Benign context (excluded from IOCs)
Standard Windows/Office/Bing/MSN telemetry, Windows Update, Adobe update check, Google Maps/Fonts, Let's Encrypt OCSP (`r10.o.lencr.org`), mDNS/SSDP discovery — all normal enterprise workstation noise, unrelated to the incident.

### Summary
Windows workstation **DESKTOP-B8TQK49** (10.11.26.183, MAC d0:57:7b:ce:fc:8b), logged in as domain user **oboomwald** on the NEMOTODES domain, was compromised with **NetSupport RAT** (signature-confirmed via C2 protocol fingerprint). The infection chain likely began with a visit to the cracked-software lure domain `modandcrackedapk.com`, after which the host began beaconing to C2 at `194.180.191.64:443` (`POST /fakeurl.htm`) and performed a NetSupport-branded geolocation check-in to `104.26.1.231`. No initial payload file or hash was recoverable from the capture since delivery occurred over encrypted TLS.
